title: The Last Benefit Period Taken to Have Fallen Due on a Healthy Options Card
content:
Which benefit period is the last to have fallen due on a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card turns on whether the card stands in use and on how long the programme has been open.

**The rule.** The last benefit period that has fallen due is the current one, where the card stands in use and at least 1 whole month has passed since the programme opened; no benefit period has fallen due, where the card does not stand in use; and it is the period before the current one in every other case.

**How the two facts are read.** The card stands in use where the programme's record carries the day the member brought it into use. The months since the programme opened are the whole months from the opening day to the day the reckoning is made.

- *Condition:* the programme record carries the day the card was brought into use, and at least 1 whole month has passed since the programme opened. *Result:* the last benefit period that has fallen due is the current one.
- *Condition:* the programme record carries no such day. *Result:* no benefit period has fallen due.
- *Condition:* the card stands in use but less than 1 whole month has passed since the programme opened. *Result:* the last benefit period that has fallen due is the period before the current one.

**Worked illustrations, on hypothetical records.** A card in use on a programme opened 5 whole months ago, where the current period is the third quarter of the year: the last period that has fallen due is that third quarter. The same card on a programme opened 12 days ago: the last period that has fallen due is the quarter before the current one. A card whose programme record shows no day of coming into use: no benefit period has fallen due at all.
